answers.answer: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest is encrypted with AES-256 or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering. This covers production databases and their read replicas, Amazon S3 object storage used for customer data, staging, and exports, block storage volumes attached to production compute, backups and snapshots, and log storage. Encryption is applied by default at the storage layer. Engineers may not create production storage with encryption disabled, and automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources. Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

Encryption at rest is applied by default at the storage layer. Engineers may not create production storage resources with encryption disabled. Automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources.

answers.answer: Yes. Every Tidewell-issued laptop must be enrolled in Tidewell's mobile device management (MDM) system and have full-disk encryption enabled, both before it is issued and at all times afterward. Laptops that fall out of compliance are flagged automatically. If a laptop is not fixed within 3 days, it loses access to corporate systems until it is compliant again.

| Device management | Enrolled in Tidewell's mobile device management (MDM) system |
| Full-disk encryption | Enabled |
Laptops that fall out of compliance are flagged automatically. If not fixed within 3 days, the laptop loses access to corporate systems until it is compliant again.
Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

answers.reasoning_note: KB-27 v1.2 (current standard, §4) directly covers both MDM enrollment and full-disk encryption, and KB-07 §3.4 also requires encryption. KB-22 and the 2024 answer library (KB-32) say the same thing but rank lower in authority.

No source mentions a bug bounty or rewards. KB-16 v1.3 §8 has a related disclosure process: reports go to security@tidewelldata.example, acknowledged within 3 business days. That doesn't confirm or rule out a bounty, so a human should answer.

No retrieved source says whether the full pentest report is shared, under NDA or otherwise. Related: the Trust Center (KB-01) lists only a "Penetration Test Summary Letter" as "On request" (KB-17, Brightline, May 2026); the SOC 2 report is the item listed as under NDA. Security team should confirm.

No passage says whether a 24/7 SOC exists or describes monitoring hours or on-call coverage. Related context: KB-06 §7 covers automated detection rules, alerts sent to the Security team's queue and escalation per the IRP; KB-10 §6.2 sets SEV1 triage within 30 minutes. Neither states 24/7 coverage.

answers.answer: Our Information Security Policy doesn't list a CISO title. The Head of Security runs the security program day to day, and the Chief Technology Officer is the accountable executive. A Security & Compliance team implements and monitors security controls, manages the SOC 2 program, and supports audits. Our documents don't name the Head of Security or give the security team's size, so those parts are unanswered.

citations.passage: **Head of Security.** Owns the security program day to day.
**Chief Technology Officer (CTO).** Accountable executive for the information security program.
**Security & Compliance team.** Implements and monitors security controls, manages the SOC 2 program, responds to customer security questionnaires, and supports audits.

answers.reasoning_note: Partial answer: current ISP v3.2 (KB-02) gives security leadership roles but no names, no CISO title, and no team size. The superseded ISP v2.4 (KB-03) and 2024 answer library (KB-32) say the Director of Engineering owned security. That is outdated and was not used.
